newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up, Shenzhen B shares down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up, Shenzhen B shares down.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up strongly on Monday with institutions buying companies which have a heavy weighting in the index, but Shenzhen B shares were dragged down by firms posting poor 1996 results, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index rose 2.572 points or 2.92 percent to 90.67 on volume of 42.673 million shares worth $23.875 million.
Brokers said both domestic and overseas institutions were seen buying on the Shanghai market due to confidence in China's economic prospects after Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule.
"Overseas investors have begun to buy on the basis of good fundamentals and improved confidence in the upward potential of B shares given China's economic development," one broker said.
Shanghai Automation Instrument was the star on its better-than-expected results, surging $0.022 or 9.82 percent to $0.246 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shanghai Chlor Alkai was the most actively traded on overseas buying, up $0.01 or 2.97 percent to $0.346 on volume of 4.4 million shares.
The Shenzhen B index lost 0.1 points or 0.06 percent to end at 176.54 on turnover of HK$273.8 million.
"Today's market was hurt by weak earnings posted by Shenzhen SEZ Real Estate and Baoshi," an analyst with China Southern Securities said.

SEZ Real Estate, a major property firm listed on Shenzhen's B share market, plunged 9.96 percent to end at HK$4.07. Over the weekend, the company posted a net loss of 26.34 million yuan for 1996 based on international accounting standards.
Despite today's slight decline in the index, optimism about the market should prevail in May, analysts said.
"Many investors believe listed companies are likely to show some improvement in their 1997 interim earnings due to China's improving economy," one analyst said.
"Expected strong debuts by some new B share listings in May are likely to boost market sentiment," another analyst said.
Nanjing Posts & Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd and Sanonda Co Ltd have said they would offer and list 100 million B shares each in Shenzhen in May.
Konka was the most actively traded Shenzhen B stock on Monday and put on HK$0.76 to HK$11.76 on volume of 3.8 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index fell on a technical correction, but trading was active with investors mixed over the market's outlook, brokers said.
The index slipped 15.047 points or 1.05 percent to 1,411.925 on volume of 845.7 million shares worth 11.9 billion yuan.
But The SSE30 blue chip index bucked the market trend on selective institutional buying, jumping 110.681 points or 2.92 percent to 3,904.495 points.
The Shenzhen A index edged up 4.4 points or 0.91 percent to close at 488.25 on turnover of 17.7 billion yuan.
